page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a network and EBS-optimized server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 64-bit Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via multithreading. The processor cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. Memory hardware comprises 21.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.62 GB of memory per virtual core. The instance includes no local storage drives and contains no GPU accelerators.

Network connectivity is a primary feature of the hardware profile, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal average multi-core CPU capacity, recording a PassMark CPU score of 8394.73 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4460.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 49.97 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 37.19 GB/sec. Performance bottlenecks occur in specialized single-threaded workloads; stress-ng single-core testing yields a weak score of 1405.39, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 27.94 GB/sec, and 7B parameter LLM prompt processing is limited to 12.14 tokens/sec.

The c5n.2xlarge provides qualitative efficiency for infrastructure requiring elevated network throughput and moderate memory density without paying for local storage disks. Its balance of 10 Gbps network bandwidth, strong Redis SET operations (7.25 million ops/sec), and 6.37 GB/sec static web throughput make it effective for web serving, database routing, intermediate caching tiers, and network appliance functions.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is an EBS- and network-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8124M processor, it offers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 21.0 GB of DDR4 RAM and 10 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The system does not include local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show balanced multi-core compute capability with a PassMark CPU score of 8394.73 and high network throughput, alongside moderate memory bandwidth of 49.97 GB/sec for uncached reads. Tradeoffs include weaker single-core processing scores and constrained throughput on LLM prompt workloads. Operating without local disk overhead, the c5n.2xlarge is structured for network-bound tasks, high-traffic web serving, and caching environments.
